# @zakkster/lite-gl

> Signal-native instanced primitive renderer. NOT a Pixi/Three competitor -- a
> narrow, zero-GC engine for one thing: project a large set of instanced primitives
> (points/quads/lines) from reactive inputs and draw them in a single instanced
> call. The killer app is a reactive chart holding ~1M points at 60fps with no
> per-frame allocation.

Peers: @zakkster/lite-signal (the reactive driver) and @zakkster/lite-raf (the
frame loop). ESM only. MIT.

## Architecture: tested core + swappable GPU sink

- GL.js (main) is the GL-AGNOSTIC core: a packed instanced-attribute buffer with
  dirty-RANGE batching, plus a reactive driver. Fully tested headlessly, including
  the 1M-point zero-GC claim.
- GLBackend.js (subpath "@zakkster/lite-gl/backend") is the WebGL2 sink. BROWSER-ONLY
  -- it calls the WebGL2 API, which has no headless context, so it is not covered by
  node:test; it is covered by a browser smoke test (by hand + Playwright in CI; see
  Coverage). Swap it for a WebGPU/canvas sink
  without touching the core.

The GPU lives behind the `sink` interface:
  upload(data, floatOffset, floatCount, instanceOffset, stride)
  draw(count)

## Honest scope

- The CORE (buffer, dirty batching, reactive projection, 1M zero-GC) is verified.
- The RENDERING (shader compile, instanced draw, 60fps at 1M) is browser-validated
  by a smoke test (manual + Playwright) -- it cannot run under node:test.
- v1.2 ships all three pipelines: POINT (scatter/particles), QUAD (bars, sized/rotated
  markers, heatmap cells), and LINE (thick polylines for line charts). All drive the
  same core via a static instanced base + vertexAttribDivisor. LINE uses butt caps only
  (perpendicular ends; a polyline is N-1 independent segments); round joins still deferred.
- v1.3 adds multi-field scenes: a per-context shared program cache, scissor panes, and an
  offscreen ID-buffer pick pass. Picking costs one extra draw PER CALL (throttle it),
  resolves overlaps last-drawn-wins, and is per-sink (call per field for cross-field picks).
- Re-projection is O(N): a camera/data change re-projects all instances. That is
  cheap on CPU; allocation is the enemy, and the pipeline is allocation-free.

## Core API (GL.js)

- createField({ capacity?, stride }) -> Field
    Field: data (Float32Array), count, capacity, push(write), set(i, write),
    swapRemove(i), setCount(n), touch(i), touchAll(), clearDirty(), dirtyLo(),
    dirtyHi(), flush(sink), reset(). `write(data, base)` fills `stride` floats.
    The backing buffer is never reallocated while you stay within capacity.
    Fails closed at construction (v1.4.1): a non-positive-integer stride, an unknown
    key (did-you-mean hint), or a capacity that is not a finite positive integer at or
    below the 2^30 hard cap throws before any allocation. capacity: 0 is rejected (it was
    an implicit default 1024 pre-1.4.1); Infinity / values past 2^30 throw rather than
    hanging nextPow2 (which is itself bounded so no input can loop it).
- reactiveField(field, { project, sink, manual? }) -> { frame, flush, stop, dispose }
    `project(field)` reads signals and writes the field; it re-runs when a tracked
    signal changes (marking the field dirty). `frame()` flushes the dirty range to
    the sink once per frame (only redraws when something changed). Auto-driven on
    lite-raf unless manual.
- createDriver(reg) -> { reactiveField }   // bind to a registry
- LAYOUT = { POINT: 8, QUAD: 9, LINE: 9 }  // floats per instance

## Backend API (GL.js/backend, browser-only)

- createPointSink(gl, { capacity }) -> { upload, draw, resize(w,h), setClearColor(r,g,b,a),
    onContextRestored(cb), isContextLost(), capacity, dispose, gl }
    Renders a LAYOUT.POINT field (x, y, size, r, g, b, a, _pad) as GL_POINTS in one
    drawArrays call. Positions are in SCREEN PIXELS -- do world->screen in `project`.
    Exposes its fixed `capacity`; an upload beyond it throws (no silent VBO/array desync).
- createQuadSink(gl, { capacity }) -> same surface as createPointSink
    Renders a LAYOUT.QUAD field (x, y, w, h, rot, r, g, b, a; stride 9) as instanced
    TRIANGLE_STRIP quads in one drawArraysInstanced call. Static unit-quad base geometry
    (loc 0, divisor 0) + per-instance attrs (loc 1..4, divisor 1) via vertexAttribDivisor.
    Same dirty-window upload, capacity guard, and context-loss recovery as points.
    Unlocks bars, sized/rotated scatter markers, and heatmap cells.
- createLineSink(gl, { capacity }) -> same surface as createPointSink
    Renders a LAYOUT.LINE field (x0, y0, x1, y1, width, r, g, b, a; stride 9) as instanced
    butt-capped thick segments. A static 4-vertex (t,s) base descriptor is expanded into a
    screen-space quad in the vertex shader from p0/p1 + width (perpendicular offset); per-
    instance attrs (loc 1..4, divisor 1). One drawArraysInstanced(TRIANGLE_STRIP) call.
    `capacity` is the number of SEGMENTS (a polyline of N points is N-1 segments). Endpoints
    and width in SCREEN PIXELS. Butt caps only in 1.2; round joins deferred to 1.3. Unlocks
    high-performance line charts, multi-series lines, step lines, and area outlines.

### Multi-field scenes + picking (v1.3)

Every sink also exposes:
- setScissor(x, y, w, h) / clearScissor()
    Clips draws AND picks to a rect: one pane of a multi-pane chart, no extra framebuffers.
    x,y are TOP-LEFT origin in device px (GL's bottom-left scissor origin is flipped for you).
- setClearColor(r, g, b, a)  (v1.4.1)
    The sink owns the clear-colour write so pick() can restore it from a JS mirror instead of
    an allocating getParameter. Route your app's clear colour through this if you want a pick
    to leave it untouched; the default (0,0,0,0) matches the GL default.
- setCounters(handle) / { counters } option  (v1.5.0)
    Optional, zero-dependency draw/upload accounting. handle is duck-typed
    { recordUpload(floatCount), recordDraw(drawCount) } -- the lite-profiler counters shape.
    recordUpload gets the dirty-window float count after each upload; recordDraw(1) fires
    after each non-empty draw. Primitive numbers only; when unset, a single truthiness guard,
    zero allocation. setCounters(null) detaches; a malformed handle throws (fail closed).
- pick(x, y, count?) -> instance index, or -1 for a miss
    Renders one ID pass into a lazily-created offscreen RGBA8 target (each instance flat-
    shaded with its index, 24-bit little-endian RGB) and reads back ONE pixel. The CPU does
    no hit-testing, so hover works at 1M instances; the GPU cost is one extra draw PER CALL,
    so call it on a throttled pointermove, never in the frame loop. Defaults to the count
    last passed to draw(). Honours the scissor, so a hover cannot hit a neighbouring pane.
    ZERO ALLOCATION (v1.4.1): restores blend (isEnabled boolean), the sink's clear colour
    (JS mirror), and the default draw framebuffer -- no allocating getParameter. Throws a
    RangeError when the top index (count-1) would reach/pass the reserved miss rather than
    aliasing it (ids must not blend). White (0xFFFFFF) is the miss value -> indices
    0..PICK_MAX_ID (0xFFFFFE) are valid, i.e. counts up to PICK_MAX_ID + 1.
    Overlaps resolve last-drawn-wins; pick is per-sink, so for cross-field picking call it on
    each field in z-order.

Programs are cached PER GL CONTEXT and refcounted: N sinks of the same primitive type in one
context share one linked program (the first pays the compile), and dispose()ing one sink
cannot delete a program another sink still holds. The cache is keyed by context because a
WebGLProgram belongs to the context that created it -- a page can hold several contexts.
A lost context drops the cache so programs relink on restore.

### Context loss (long-running overlays)

A GL context is lost eventually (GPU reset, driver update, tab backgrounded on
mobile). The sink owns recovery: it listens for webglcontextlost/restored on
gl.canvas, no-ops draw/upload while lost, and rebuilds program + VBO + VAO on
restore. The restored buffer is EMPTY, so onContextRestored(cb) lets you re-upload;
reactiveField wires field.touchAll() + flush automatically when the sink exposes
the hook, so the image returns on its own. isContextLost() reflects the state.

### Coverage

No headless WebGL2 exists, so the backend has two coverage layers. (1) node:test
against a MOCK WebGL2 context (test/GLBackend_test.mjs): the GL call sequence of the
POINT, QUAD, and LINE sinks -- compile/link, one-time VBO sizing, instance attributes +
vertexAttribDivisor, dirty-window bufferSubData, the drawArrays / drawArraysInstanced
call, capacity guard, and teardown -- plus an end-to-end pass driving the GL.js core
through each sink. (2) A browser smoke test for the real GPU pixels: test/smoke.html
(pixel readback -- non-blank, position mapping, dirty-window upload, context-loss
recovery), runnable by hand in any browser, and test/smoke.spec.mjs under Playwright
(headless Chromium = WebGL2 via SwiftShader) for CI. The core's re-seed-on-restore
wiring also has a node:test mock-sink case. The v1.3 surface is covered by the same mock:
the shared program cache (N sinks -> 1 linkProgram), per-context isolation, refcounted dispose,
scissor y-flip, and the pick pass (24-bit decode, miss = -1, out-of-bounds short-circuit,
blend disabled during the ID pass, framebuffer/clear-colour/blend restored, scissor honoured).

## Composition

- Camera: project from a @zakkster/lite-camera-max view, so pan/zoom is a signal and
  the camera lives in the reactive graph; the shader only maps pixels to clip space.
- Charts: this is the renderer @zakkster/lite-charts reaches for past the Canvas2D
  ceiling (~tens of thousands) to hundreds of thousands / millions of points.

## Zero-GC

A frame re-projects in place and uploads only the dirty float window -- no
allocation. Verified: 60 frames of full 1M-point re-projection with the backing
Float32Array reference unchanged and the engine pool counters flat.

## v2.0.0 -- the WebGPU sink

export const VERSION = "2.0.0" (package.json + GL.js + llms.txt kept in lockstep).

WEBGPU BACKEND (subpath "@zakkster/lite-gl/webgpu", GLWebGPU.js). A SECOND GPU sink that
mirrors the WebGL2 sink interface exactly (upload/draw + resize/setScissor/clearScissor/
setClearColor/setCounters/onContextRestored/isContextLost/dispose/pick) and drives the same
GL.js core unchanged. The field byte layout is BYTE-IDENTICAL to WebGL2 (POINT 8, QUAD 9,
LINE 9, POINT_HI 10); only the rendering MECHANISM differs -- WebGPU has no gl_PointSize, so
POINT/POINT_HI are instanced unit-quads expanded by a_size in the vertex shader (the pick
pass widens the same way). WGSL lives inline. Proven headlessly (an injected mock GPUDevice +
a precision-parity suite + torture WebGPU tiers); real-GPU validation runs in CI via the
`webgpu` project of test/smoke.spec.mjs (test/smoke.html?scene=webgpu) where a WebGPU adapter
is available, and records an explicit skip otherwise.

  await createGPUTarget(canvas, { device? , format? , alphaMode? , reacquire? }) -> target
    Acquires navigator.gpu.requestAdapter()/requestDevice() (or takes an injected { device })
    and configures the context. FAILS CLOSED: absent navigator.gpu, a null adapter, or a
    rejected device all THROW -- never a null/degraded sink. Owns device.lost + restore().
  createGPUPointSink / createGPUPointHiSink / createGPUQuadSink / createGPULineSink(target,
    { capacity, counters?, blend? }) -> sink   // same four primitives as WebGL2.

BLEND (opt-in, baked at construction). opts.blend = "opaque" (default) / "additive" / "alpha".
WebGPU owns blend in the render PIPELINE, so the mode is resolved ONCE (cold) and consumed only
when the DRAW pipeline is built -- the hot bodies (upload/draw/pick) never read or branch on it.
Contrast the WebGL2 sink, which leaves blend to whatever the GL context has enabled. The PICK
pipeline is ALWAYS opaque for every mode (blending the 24-bit id would corrupt the decode). An
unknown mode THROWS with a did-you-mean hint before any device resource is created (fail closed).
The normalized mode is exposed as the read-only sink.blend string (introspection; not a caps flag).

CAPS. caps = { api:"webgpu", instancing:true, baseVertex:true, maxInstances:0xFFFFFF (=
PICK_MAX_ID+1, identical to WebGL2), precisionHi:<per-sink>, pickMode:"deferred", version:1 }.
Same key set/order as the WebGL2 caps; precisionHi true ONLY on createGPUPointHiSink.

DEFERRED PICK (the second v2.0.0 break, on pickMode:"deferred" sinks only). WebGPU has no
synchronous readPixels, so pick(x,y,count) renders a 24-bit-id pass (rgba8unorm, EXACT
r|g<<8|b<<16 decode + 0xFFFFFF miss sentinel, so PICK_MAX_ID stays meaningful and identical
on both backends), copies one texel into a pooled readback buffer (ring depth K=2), and
returns PICK_PENDING (-2) until the async mapAsync resolves; a later identical pick() returns
the decoded index (>=0) or -1 (miss). Both ring slots in flight -> PICK_PENDING back-pressure,
no unbounded queue, zero per-call steady-state allocation. A "sync" WebGL2 sink NEVER returns
PICK_PENDING. PICK_PENDING is exported from GL.js and re-exported from GLWebGPU.js.

ZERO-GC. The WebGPU sink adds ZERO per-frame JS allocation (every render-pass descriptor and
the submit array are preallocated and mutated in place); all per-frame cost is at the device
boundary (createCommandEncoder/beginRenderPass/submit), gated deterministically by
test/gates/webgpu-frame-alloc.mjs at 192 B/frame (a property of the mock, zero tolerance). The
core's project/flush contribution nets < 1.0 B/op on BOTH sinks (torture T6/T6(gpu)). Precision:
the POINT_HI camera port is BIT-EXACT WGSL-vs-GLSL over the Fork B' vectors (test/precision_
parity_test.mjs).

## v2.0.0 -- the caps seam (the first intended breaking surface)

The caps seam landed under the v2.0.0 line (package.json + GL.js + llms.txt kept in lockstep).

CAPS SEAM (GL8a). Every sink now advertises a FROZEN caps descriptor:

  caps = { api:"webgl2", instancing:true, baseVertex:false, maxInstances:0xFFFFFF,
           precisionHi:<per-sink>, pickMode:"sync", version:1 }

precisionHi is true ONLY on createPointHiSink; the other three advertise false. pickMode
is "sync" on all four WebGL2 sinks. maxInstances (0xFFFFFF) aligns with PICK_MAX_ID + 1.

reactiveField reads sink.caps EXACTLY ONCE, at bind, via assertCaps, and fails closed:
a sink with no caps throws; a LAYOUT.POINT_HI field bound to a non-precisionHi sink throws;
a field whose capacity exceeds caps.maxInstances throws with a size hint. The per-frame
closure reads NO caps -- the hot path (upload/draw/pickAt/flush/push/set/swapRemove) is
byte-unchanged from v1.5.0 and is fenced by test/hash_parity.mjs. THE BREAK: a custom sink
must now expose a caps object; a sink without one no longer binds.

## v1.5.0 -- the counters seam (lite-profiler) + the zero-tolerance dirty-range gate

export const VERSION = "1.5.0" was the prior lockstep version (package.json + GL.js + llms.txt).

COUNTERS SEAM (GL6). Every WebGL2 sink takes an OPTIONAL, zero-dependency counters
handle -- duck-typed { recordUpload(floatCount), recordDraw(drawCount) }, exactly the
shape @zakkster/lite-profiler 1.2.0 exposes -- and emits the two draw/upload metrics
into it. lite-profiler stays a PEER/optional integration, never a runtime dependency
(package.json dependencies is empty). Attach it two ways:

  const sink = createPointSink(gl, { capacity, counters: prof.counters });  // at construction
  sink.setCounters(prof.counters);   // or later; setCounters(null) detaches

On each frame the sink calls counters.recordUpload(floatCount) after a bufferSubData
(the dirty-window float count) and counters.recordDraw(1) after each non-empty draw.
PRIMITIVE NUMBERS only -- no per-call object. When no counters are attached the guard is
a single truthiness check and the path allocates nothing: the core hot functions
(field.flush, writePointHi) are byte-identical to v1.4.1 (SHA parity holds), and the
torture T8 zero-alloc gate is green both WITH and WITHOUT counters attached (0 B/op).
A bad handle (non-null, missing recordUpload/recordDraw) throws at attach time (fail closed).

DIRTY-RANGE GATE (GL7). test/gates/dirty-range.mjs is a headless, GPU-free build gate:
a deterministic op stream (append N, scatter-edit K single instances each flushed,
swap-remove M) runs against a mock sink that sums floatsUploaded, and the total is
asserted against a COMMITTED baseline constant at ZERO tolerance. A regression where a
one-instance edit re-uploads the whole buffer changes the total by thousands of floats
and fails the build with no GPU required. The file carries a self-control that simulates
that full-buffer regression and confirms the gate goes red. Run via `npm run test:gates`
(also folded into `npm test`). To change the dirty-range contract deliberately, update
the BASELINE constant in the file in the same commit.

## v1.4.1 -- shipped surface fixes + fail-closed hardening + zero-alloc pick + the torture gate

- GL.d.ts now compiles under default tsc: removed a duplicate LAYOUT block (TS2451). The
  surviving block carries POINT_HI: 10.
- README headline install fixed: import from the exported "@zakkster/lite-gl/backend" subpath
  (the raw backend filename is not in the exports map).
- export const VERSION = "1.4.1" added to GL.js (version now in package.json + GL.js + llms.txt).

FAIL CLOSED (GL2). Validation lives at construction only; the hot bodies gain zero branches.
- createField now rejects a non-positive-integer stride (throws naming the LAYOUT strides),
  an unknown key (throws with a did-you-mean, e.g. strid -> stride), and a capacity present
  but not positive. capacity: 0 was previously an implicit "use default 1024" and is now
  rejected as a degenerate input (null is not zero).
- reactiveField().flush() after dispose() is a no-op (mirrors the frame() guard).
- flush clamps a post-shrink stale dirty range to [dLo, min(dHi, count-1)] -- never uploads
  past the active count. No allocation.
- pick() throws a RangeError over PICK_MAX_ID (0xFFFFFE) instead of aliasing the reserved miss.

ZERO-ALLOC PICK (GL3). pickAt no longer calls getParameter(COLOR_CLEAR_VALUE) (a fresh
Float32Array every call). Clear colour is restored from the sink's JS mirror -- set it with
the new sink.setClearColor(r, g, b, a) (the sink owns the write) -- blend from the
non-allocating isEnabled boolean, and the picker's ensure() result object is reused. Measured
0 B/op over 100k picks per layout. Pick correctness (decode/miss/oob/state-restore) unchanged.

- test/torture.mjs: the node --expose-gc gate (lite-leak + lite-gc-profiler). Tiers
  T0/T1/T2/T3/T4/T5/T6/T7/T9. `npm run test:torture`. T6 proves bytes-per-op == 0 and
  maxMajor == 0 over 1M frames of project+flush+draw AND the now-real pick sub-gate for
  POINT/POINT_HI/QUAD/LINE; T3 grows across a pow2 boundary mid-dirty-range; T4 covers
  post-dispose flush, double-dispose, context-loss re-seed and program-cache refcount; T5 is
  a differential fuzz vs a naive full-upload oracle; T7 is the 1M soak + create/dispose
  conservation.

NOTE: hot-path change, intentional and gated. pickAt was rewritten (GL-05) and flush gained
the N-3 clamp -- both SHAs change. project/push/set/writePointHi executable logic is
unchanged from v1.4.0 (only an inline writePointHi comment was softened).

## v1.4.0 — deep-zoom precision (LAYOUT.POINT_HI + createPointHiSink)

THE CONTRACT (now explicit). LAYOUT.POINT / QUAD / LINE hold SCREEN PIXELS. project() runs in
JS float64 and writes post-camera pixel coordinates, so the float32 field only ever sees small
numbers — relative-to-eye by construction. Precision is a non-issue. The cost: every camera
change re-projects every instance on the CPU and re-uploads the dirty range (~5 ms + 31 MB per
frame at 1M points).

LAYOUT.POINT_HI (stride 10: xHi, yHi, xLo, yLo, size, r, g, b, a, _pad) holds WORLD coordinates,
uploaded once, with the camera in the vertex shader. A pan is sink.setCamera(x, y, sx, sy, px, py)
— four floats of uniform, zero CPU, zero upload.

WHY DOUBLE-EMULATION. float32 has a 24-bit significand: integers exact only to 2^24 = 16,777,216.
Epoch-ms is ~1.78e12 -> ULP = 131,072 ms ≈ 2.2 minutes. A minute of 1-second ticks collapses onto
ONE float32 value. Epoch-seconds is no escape (ULP ~128 s).

THE SCHEME. Split each float64 coord into hi = fround(v) and lo = fround(v - hi). The shader does
  rel = (a_posHi - u_cameraHi) + (a_posLo - u_cameraLo)
The high parts are float32s of near-identical magnitude, so the subtraction cancels EXACTLY
(Sterbenz lemma) and the residuals carry the detail. Do NOT reorder this — scale first, subtract
later, and the precision is already gone. `precision highp float` is required.

THE GUARANTEE. Error scales with distance FROM THE EYE, not absolute magnitude. Bit-exact within
a day of the camera at epoch-ms; ~800 ms error a year out — which is fine, because you only see
distant points when zoomed out and the pixel grows at the same rate. Worst-case sub-pixel error
across a 2000px viewport: ~1e-4 px, at ANY zoom, at ANY absolute magnitude.

HELPERS (GL.js, GL-agnostic):
  writePointHi(data, base, x, y, size, r, g, b, a)  — packs one instance, does the split, zero alloc
  hiOf(v) / loOf(v)                                 — the split; hiOf(v) + loOf(v) === v exactly
  f32Ulp(v)                                         — float32 quantization step at magnitude v
  needsHiPrecision(maxAbsCoord, resolution)         — "do I need this layout?" guardrail
                                                      needsHiPrecision(Date.now(), 1000) === true

PICKING. The ID pass pushes the SAME camera uniforms as the visible pass. It must — otherwise the
pixel you read back belongs to a different instance than the one under the cursor.

CAMERAS. lite-gl deliberately has NO camera dependency, peer or otherwise. setCamera(x, y, sx, sy,
px, py) takes six plain numbers -- drive it from whatever owns your pan/zoom state.
@zakkster/lite-camera is a game-follow camera for Canvas2D (deadzone, lookahead, trauma shake,
clamped to a world rect, emits a ctx transform). It has NO zoom, pins x >= 0, and its apply() does
ctx.translate(-(pos[0] | 0), ...) -- a ToInt32 truncation that WRAPS at epoch-ms magnitudes. Correct
for a platformer, wrong for a chart. lite-camera-pro adds five more deps on top. Do not couple them.

WHEN TO USE WHICH. POINT for anything that fits comfortably in float32 after projection (almost
everything). POINT_HI when the WORLD coordinates are large: timestamps, geodetic coords, deep-zoom
fractals — or when you pan/zoom a large field often enough that CPU re-projection is the bottleneck.
